answer: Each new agent's first voyage into the network triggers peer-issued micro-benchmarks: three verifiers send distinct random matrix tasks with 90-second wall-clock deadlines, each seeded from a fresh nonce so answers cannot be pre-shared. A clone farm time-sharing one GPU cannot finish three independent deadlines without slowing the vine of dependent proofs, and timing gaps surface as a measurable ripple across latency fingerprints. First mismatch flags the identity; second freezes emission and routes it to manual review. Faking 5000 identities needs 15000 GPU-seconds, about $4000 daily.
